chunks: Ahmad b. al-Hasan al-Qattan narrated to us. He said: al-Abbas b. al-Fadl b. Shadhan al-Muqri narrated to us. He said: Ja'far b. Muhammad b. Harun narrated to us from Uzra al-Qattan. He said: Mas'ud Abu Abdillah al-Khiladi narrated to us. He said: Tulayd narrated to me from Abi'l Hijaf from Abi Idris from Mujahid from Ali (as). He said: The Messenger of Allah (s) said to me:
O Ali! Whoever splits away from you has split away from me; and whoever splits away from me has split away from Allah, the Mighty and Majestic.

key_terms.عزوجل: the Mighty and Majestic — a reverential epithet for Allah
key_terms.فارقك: splits from you — separating oneself from Ali's guidance and authority
key_terms.فارقني: splits from me — separating from the Prophet's path

ai.seo_question: What did Prophet Muhammad say about separating from Ali?
ai.summary: The Prophet (s) directly addresses Imam Ali (as), equating separation from Ali with separation from the Prophet himself, and separation from the Prophet with separation from Allah. This hadith, narrated through a chain reaching Mujahid the Meccan exegete, is a powerful statement on the inseparable bond between Ali and the Prophet, and through the Prophet, with God Himself. Such narrations were used by early Shia scholars to establish Ali's authority as the rightful successor.

en.bilal-muhammad: Ahmad b. al-Hasan al-Qattan narrated to us. He said: al-`Abbas b. al-Fadl b. Shadhan al-Muqri narrated to us. He said: Ja`far b. Muhammad b. Harun narrated to us from `Uzra al-Qattan. He said: Mas`ud Abu `Abdillah al-Khiladi narrate to us. He said: Tulayd narrated to me from Abi’l Hijaf from Abi Idris from Mujahid from `Ali (as). He said: The Messenger of Allah (s) said to me:
O `Ali! Whoever splits away from you has split away from me; and whoever splits away from me has split away from Allah.
